primary_evidence: linux-ci-44144974913: clean baseline and candidate builds, one hosted runner, seeded interleaved variants, three independent 5-second cases per group
limits: Windows baseline environment observes a dirty tool workspace at 8ecb2aa while plan.server_binary points to the separately built v0.1.7 baseline; that observed source tree is not proven to be the binary build source.
Windows candidate records a non-clean tool workspace and a separately asserted product revision; binary hashes are retained, but neither Windows dataset is a clean-commit build comparison.
All binaries print ling 0.1.7 because product version had not yet been bumped; compare commit and binary hashes, not the version text alone.
Windows Reliable is unsupported and skipped, never counted as a pass.
Latency values are nearest-rank quantiles recomputed from each individual raw gzip. Repetitions are not pooled; reported median/min/max summarize the three per-run values.
Idle scenarios measure serial closed-loop PING latency with 0, 1 or 100 idle subscriptions; backlog measures confirmed EVENT ACK throughput and has no request latency samples.
Each measurement lasts about five seconds. Three repeats do not establish statistical significance, sustained capacity, physical durability, or target deployment performance.
Linux CI filesystem reports ext4 data=writeback,nobarrier,journal_async_commit; Reliable figures include software fsync calls but establish no physical power-loss guarantee.

Linux process CPU deltas are primary CPU evidence; some Windows CPU readings are zero while others are nonzero; short-sample resolution and shared scheduling prevent treating zero as evidence of zero CPU cost.

analysis: Linux notification=on removes measured idle dispatch polls (all repeats: 0); legacy/off retain about 500 polls per idle subscriber over five seconds.
Linux on PING P99/P99.9 has no consistent tail-latency degradation in these runs; idle-100 tails improve, while PING throughput decreases and must be reported separately.

Linux backlog on confirmed-ACK throughput is about 52% below legacy in both Fast and Reliable, consistently in every repeat. Functional acceptance alone therefore does not establish performance acceptance.

Linux off backlog throughput is close to legacy and restores the measured polling behavior. At idle-100, off P99/P99.9 is moderately higher than legacy across all three repeats; no exact performance equivalence is claimed.

Windows Fast on backlog is much faster than legacy/off, unlike Linux. Windows idle-100 on P99.9 is higher than legacy in all three repeats; the identity and scheduling limitations make it supporting evidence, not an override of Linux results.

Backlog notification=on starts and ends measurement with the 128-event pending window full. Legacy/off start with about 5-13 pending and end with about 3-7; this is an observed scheduling difference, not proof of packet-level causality.

No per-ACK timestamps or packet capture exist in the frozen backlog data. The repeat-level ACK rates support the throughput regression, but no backlog latency curve, TCP Nagle attribution, or fsync-delay attribution can be derived from these artifacts.
